bigIdea: Bread rises because yeast makes gas and gluten traps it, so when you control time and temperature, you control the loaf.

beats.name: Orientation
beats.claim: A dense loaf is a timing problem, not a recipe problem.

beats.name: Foundations
beats.claim: Yeast makes the gas, gluten traps it, and warmth sets the pace.

beats.name: Application
beats.claim: Read the dough, not the clock: the poke test tells you when it is ready.

beats.name: Mastery
beats.claim: A cold kitchen needs more time, not more yeast.

beats.name: Assessment
beats.claim: You can tell an underproofed loaf from an overproofed one by its crumb.

beats.name: Transfer
beats.claim: Bake one loaf this week and change only the rise time.
